title: Complete RNA-seq Analysis Workflow with VISTA
text: vignette demonstrates complete RNA-seq differential expression workflow using VISTA (Visualization Integrated System Transcriptomic Analysis). ’ll use well-known airway dataset Bioconductor, contains RNA-seq data airway smooth muscle cells treated dexamethasone.

title: Complete RNA-seq Analysis Workflow with VISTA
text: VISTA streamlines RNA-seq analysis : Unifying DE workflows: Wraps DESeq2 edgeR consistent output Simplifying visualization: 28+ publication-ready plotting functions Integrating enrichment: Built-MSigDB, GO, KEGG analysis Ensuring reproducibility: S4 class structure comprehensive metadata

title: Complete RNA-seq Analysis Workflow with VISTA
text: airway dataset (Himes et al. 2014) includes: Samples: 8 human airway smooth muscle cell lines Treatment: 4 treated dexamethasone, 4 untreated Sequencing: Illumina HiSeq 2000 Features: ~64,000 genes Reference: Himes et al. (2014). “RNA-Seq transcriptome profiling identifies CRISPLD2 glucocorticoid responsive gene modulates cytokine function airway smooth muscle cells.” PLoS One 9(6): e99625.

title: Complete RNA-seq Analysis Workflow with VISTA
text: VISTA requires count data.frame gene ID column: Prepare sample info proper rownames:
code: # Create count data.frame with gene_id column count_data <- as.data.frame(counts_matrix) %>% tibble::as_tibble() count_data$gene_id <- rownames(counts_matrix)  # Reorder columns: gene_id first, then samples count_data <- count_data[, c("gene_id", colnames(counts_matrix))]  # Preview count_data[1:5, 1:5] #> # A tibble: 5 × 5 #>   gene_id         SRR1039508 SRR1039509 SRR1039512 SRR1039513 #>   <chr>                <int>      <int>      <int>      <int> #> 1 ENSG00000000003        679        448        873        408 #> 2 ENSG00000000005          0          0          0          0 #> 3 ENSG00000000419        467        515        621        365 #> 4 ENSG00000000457        260        211        263        164 #> 5 ENSG00000000460         60         55         40         35 # Sample info must have rownames matching count column names sample_info <- sample_metadata %>%   tibble::as_tibble() %>%   dplyr::rename("sample_names" = "Run") %>%   dplyr::mutate(sample_names = as.character(sample_names))  # Key columns for VISTA sample_info[, c("sample_names", "cell", "treatment", "dex")] #> # A tibble: 8 × 4 #>   sample_names cell    treatment     dex   #>   <chr>        <fct>   <chr>         <fct> #> 1 SRR1039508   N61311  Untreated     untrt #> 2 SRR1039509   N61311  Dexamethasone trt   #> 3 SRR1039512   N052611 Untreated     untrt #> 4 SRR1039513   N052611 Dexamethasone trt   #> 5 SRR1039516   N080611 Untreated     untrt #> 6 SRR1039517   N080611 Dexamethasone trt   #> 7 SRR1039520   N061011 Untreated     untrt #> 8 SRR1039521   N061011 Dexamethasone trt

title: Complete RNA-seq Analysis Workflow with VISTA
text: primary method creating VISTA object: VISTA object stores: Normalized counts assays Sample metadata colData Gene annotations rowData DE results metadata
code: # Create VISTA object with DESeq2 backend vista <- create_vista(   counts = count_data,   sample_info = sample_info,   column_geneid = "gene_id",   group_column = "treatment",   group_numerator = "Dexamethasone",   group_denominator = "Untreated",   method = "deseq2",   min_counts = 10,   min_replicates = 2,   log2fc_cutoff = 1.0,   pval_cutoff = 0.05,   p_value_type = "padj" )  # Examine the VISTA object vista #> class: VISTA  #> dim: 17199 8  #> metadata(12): de_results de_summary ... design comparison #> assays(1): norm_counts #> rownames(17199): ENSG00000000003 ENSG00000000419 ... ENSG00000273487 #>   ENSG00000273488 #> rowData names(1): baseMean #> colnames(8): SRR1039508 SRR1039509 ... SRR1039520 SRR1039521 #> colData names(11): SampleName cell ... sizeFactor sample_names

title: Complete RNA-seq Analysis Workflow with VISTA
text: create_vista() runs validation default (validate = TRUE). can also run explicitly: advanced users importing pre-built SummarizedExperiment, use as_vista() validate:
code: validate_vista(vista, level = "full") se <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(   assays = list(norm_counts = norm_counts(vista)),   colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_info(vista), row.names = sample_info(vista)$sample_names),   rowData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(row_data(vista), row.names = rownames(norm_counts(vista))) ) vista2 <- as_vista(se, group_column = "treatment") validate_vista(vista2, level = "full")

what: Advanced: covariates, design formula, and consensus mode
title: Complete RNA-seq Analysis Workflow with VISTA
code: # Covariate-adjusted model (additive design) vista_cov <- create_vista(   counts = count_data,   sample_info = sample_info,   column_geneid = "gene_id",   group_column = "treatment",   group_numerator = "Dexamethasone",   group_denominator = "Untreated",   method = "deseq2",   covariates = c("cell") )  # Equivalent explicit model formula vista_formula <- create_vista(   counts = count_data,   sample_info = sample_info,   column_geneid = "gene_id",   group_column = "treatment",   group_numerator = "Dexamethasone",   group_denominator = "Untreated",   method = "deseq2",   design_formula = "~ cell + treatment" )  # Run both DESeq2 and edgeR and keep consensus as active source vista_both <- create_vista(   counts = count_data,   sample_info = sample_info,   column_geneid = "gene_id",   group_column = "treatment",   group_numerator = "Dexamethasone",   group_denominator = "Untreated",   method = "both",   consensus_mode = "intersection",  # or "union"   result_source = "consensus"       # or "deseq2"/"edger" )  # Access source-specific outputs comparisons(vista_both, source = "consensus") comparisons(vista_both, source = "deseq2") comparisons(vista_both, source = "edger")  # Switch the active source used by plotting functions vista_both <- set_de_source(vista_both, "edger")

code: # Pathway-coloured chord diagram (no VISTA object needed) if (!is.null(msig_up$enrich) && nrow(msig_up$enrich@result) > 0) {   get_enrichment_chord(     msig_up,     top_n    = 6,     color_by = "pathway",     title    = "Gene-Pathway Membership (Up-regulated, Hallmark)"   ) } # Fold-change coloured chords if (!is.null(msig_up$enrich) && nrow(msig_up$enrich@result) > 0) {   get_enrichment_chord(     msig_up,     vista  = vista,     sample_comparison = names(comparisons(vista))[1],     top_n      = 6,     color_by   = "foldchange",     display_id = "SYMBOL",     title      = "Gene-Pathway Chord (coloured by log2FC)"   ) } # Show only hub genes shared across 2+ pathways if (!is.null(msig_up$enrich) && nrow(msig_up$enrich@result) > 0) {   chord_result <- get_enrichment_chord(     msig_up,     vista    = vista,     sample_comparison   = names(comparisons(vista))[1],     top_n        = 8,     min_pathways = 2,     color_by     = "regulation",     display_id   = "SYMBOL",     title        = "Hub Genes Bridging Multiple Pathways"   )    # Inspect hub genes returned invisibly   if (length(chord_result$hub_genes)) {     cat("Hub genes:", paste(head(chord_result$hub_genes, 10), collapse = ", "), "\n")   } } #> Hub genes: ENSG00000003402, ENSG00000060718, ENSG00000067082, ENSG00000099860, ENSG00000102804, ENSG00000118689, ENSG00000120129, ENSG00000122641, ENSG00000130066, ENSG00000131979

title: Enrichment Chord Diagrams with VISTA
text: Functional enrichment analysis (MSigDB, GO, KEGG) returns table significant pathways. standard dot plot bar plot answers “pathways enriched?” – hides two critical questions: genes drive multiple enriched pathways? handful “hub genes” often appear 3–5 enriched terms simultaneously. genes disproportionately important interpreting results, yet invisible standard enrichment dot plot. redundant top pathways? top 8 pathways share 15 genes, 8 independent biological signals – one signal reported 8 times. dot plot reveal ; chord diagram can.

title: Enrichment Chord Diagrams with VISTA
text: Enrichment results many--many structure: genes belong multiple pathways, pathways share genes. relational data – natural visualization chord diagram : - Sectors represent pathways (one side) genes () - Chords connect gene pathways belongs - Chord colour encodes fold-change direction magnitude fundamentally different genome-positional plots (circular layout cosmetic) connections data.

title: Enrichment Chord Diagrams with VISTA
text: create basic enrichment chord diagram get_enrichment_chord() colour chords pathway membership, regulation direction, continuous fold-change isolate hub genes – genes shared across multiple pathways control visual output publication-ready figures

title: Enrichment Chord Diagrams with VISTA
text: use airway dataset (Himes et al. 2014) – RNA-seq human airway smooth muscle cells treated dexamethasone. dataset used main VISTA workflow vignette.
code: library(airway) library(org.Hs.eg.db)  data("airway", package = "airway")  # Extract counts and sample info counts_matrix <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(airway, "counts") sample_metadata <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(airway)) sample_metadata$treatment <- ifelse(   sample_metadata$dex == "trt", "Dexamethasone", "Untreated" )  count_data <- as.data.frame(counts_matrix) %>% tibble::as_tibble() count_data$gene_id <- rownames(counts_matrix) count_data <- count_data[, c("gene_id", colnames(counts_matrix))]  sample_info <- sample_metadata %>%   tibble::as_tibble() %>%   dplyr::rename("sample_names" = "Run") %>%   dplyr::mutate(sample_names = as.character(sample_names))

title: Enrichment Chord Diagrams with VISTA
code: vista <- create_vista(   counts       = count_data,   sample_info  = sample_info,   column_geneid = "gene_id",   group_column     = "treatment",   group_numerator  = "Dexamethasone",   group_denominator = "Untreated",   method       = "deseq2",   min_counts   = 10,   min_replicates = 2,   log2fc_cutoff = 1.0,   pval_cutoff   = 0.05,   p_value_type  = "padj" )  vista <- set_rowdata(   vista,   orgdb   = org.Hs.eg.db,   columns = c("SYMBOL", "GENENAME", "ENTREZID"),   keytype = "ENSEMBL" )  vista #> class: VISTA  #> dim: 17199 8  #> metadata(12): de_results de_summary ... design comparison #> assays(1): norm_counts #> rownames(17199): ENSG00000000003 ENSG00000000419 ... code: if (!is.null(msig_hallmark$enrich) && nrow(msig_hallmark$enrich@result) > 0) {   hub_result <- get_enrichment_chord(     msig_hallmark,     vista    = vista,     sample_comparison   = comp_name,     top_n        = 8,     min_pathways = 2,     color_by     = "foldchange",     display_id   = "SYMBOL",     title        = "Hub genes only (shared across 2+ pathways)"   )    cat("Hub genes found:", length(hub_result$hub_genes), "\n")   cat("Genes:", paste(head(hub_result$hub_genes, 20), collapse = ", "), "\n") } #> Hub genes found: 43  #> Genes: ENSG00000003402, ENSG00000060718, ENSG00000067082, ENSG00000085117, ENSG00000099860, ENSG00000100292, ENSG00000102804, ENSG00000105835, ENSG00000108821, ENSG00000112715, ENSG00000117152, ENSG00000118689, ENSG00000120129, ENSG00000122641, ENSG00000123610, ENSG00000124762, ENSG00000125657, ENSG00000128342, ENSG00000130066, ENSG00000131979

text: Pass named colour vector override default HCL palette:
code: if (!is.null(msig_hallmark$enrich) && nrow(msig_hallmark$enrich@result) > 0) {   # Get the top pathway names first   top_pathways <- head(msig_hallmark$enrich@result$Description, 5)    # Define custom colors   custom_cols <- c(     "#264653", "#2A9D8F", "#E9C46A", "#F4A261", "#E76F51"   )   names(custom_cols) <- top_pathways    get_enrichment_chord(     msig_hallmark,     top_n          = 5,     color_by       = "pathway",     pathway_colors = custom_cols,     title          = "Custom pathway colours"   ) }

text: Fine-tune gap size, label size, transparency:
code: if (!is.null(msig_hallmark$enrich) && nrow(msig_hallmark$enrich@result) > 0) {   get_enrichment_chord(     msig_hallmark,     top_n        = 5,     color_by     = "pathway",     gap_degree   = 4,          # wider gaps between sectors     label_cex    = 0.6,        # smaller labels     transparency = 0.2,        # more opaque chords     title        = "Adjusted layout"   ) }

code: if (!is.null(msig_hallmark$enrich) && nrow(msig_hallmark$enrich@result) > 0) {   available <- msig_hallmark$enrich@result$Description   # Pick specific pathways of interest (if available)   pick <- intersect(     c("HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY",       "HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB",       "HALLMARK_HYPOXIA",       "HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS"),     available   )    if (length(pick) >= 2) {     get_enrichment_chord(       msig_hallmark,       pathways   = pick,       vista  = vista,       sample_comparison = comp_name,       color_by   = "foldchange",       display_id = "SYMBOL",       title      = "Selected pathways of interest"     )   } }

title: Code Economy: VISTA vs. Standard R Workflows
text: standard RNA-seq differential expression analysis – raw counts publication-ready figures enrichment results – requires assembling 6–10 packages, data structures, naming conventions, implicit assumptions. user responsible : Data plumbing: converting DESeqDataSet, DGEList, data frames, matrices, tibbles every interface boundary Identifier management: gene IDs must stripped, mapped, re-mapped stage (DE, annotation, enrichment, visualisation) State tracking: cutoffs, method settings, comparison names, color schemes scattered across script variables structured persistence Visual consistency: colours, axis labels, themes must manually coordinated across dozens ggplot2 calls None steps involve scientific reasoning. engineering overhead. VISTA eliminates . vignette makes claim concrete: perform analysis twice data – standard packages, VISTA – measure difference.

title: Code Economy: VISTA vs. Standard R Workflows
text: use airway dataset (Himes et al. 2014): 8 samples human airway smooth muscle cells, 4 treated dexamethasone, 4 untreated.
code: library(airway) library(org.Hs.eg.db)  data("airway", package = "airway")  counts_matrix <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(airway, "counts") sample_meta   <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(airway)) sample_meta$treatment <- ifelse(sample_meta$dex == "trt", "Dexamethasone", "Untreated")

title: Code Economy: VISTA vs. Standard R Workflows
text: code uses established Bioconductor CRAN packages – DESeq2, ggplot2, ComplexHeatmap, clusterProfiler, msigdbr, AnnotationDbi. representative real analysis scripts found published supplementary materials. 9 library calls single line analysis.
code: library(DESeq2) library(ggplot2) library(ggrepel) library(dplyr) library(tibble) library(clusterProfiler) library(msigdbr) library(AnnotationDbi) library(org.Hs.eg.db)

title: Code Economy: VISTA vs. Standard R Workflows
text: 18 lines. user must know: DESeqDataSetFromMatrix, formula syntax, manual filtering logic, results() contrast specification, fold-change p-value cutoff application, regulation classification.
code: # Build DESeqDataSet dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(   countData = counts_matrix,   colData   = sample_meta,   design    = ~ treatment )  # Filter low-count genes keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= 2 dds  <- dds[keep, ]  # Run DE pipeline dds <- DESeq(dds)  # Extract results res <- results(dds, contrast = c("treatment", "Dexamethasone", "Untreated")) res_df <- as.data.frame(res) %>%   rownames_to_column("gene_id") %>%   mutate(     regulation = case_when(       log2FoldChange >=  1 & padj < 0.05 ~ "Up",       log2FoldChange <= -1 & padj < 0.05 ~ "Down",       TRUE ~ "Other"     )   )  # Get normalized counts for downstream plots norm_mat <- counts(dds, normalized = TRUE)

title: Code Economy: VISTA vs. Standard R Workflows
text: 8 lines. user must handle mapIds(), know correct keytype, deal multi-mapping.
code: # Map Ensembl IDs to gene symbols gene_symbols <- mapIds(   org.Hs.eg.db,   keys    = res_df$gene_id,   keytype = "ENSEMBL",   column  = "SYMBOL",   multiVals = "first" )  res_df$SYMBOL <- gene_symbols[res_df$gene_id]

title: Code Economy: VISTA vs. Standard R Workflows
text: 14 lines. user must know: vst(), plotPCA() returnData, extract percent variance attributes, manual ggplot2 construction, hardcoded colour assignment.
code: # Variance-stabilising transform vsd <- vst(dds, blind = FALSE)  # Extract PCA data pca_data <- plotPCA(vsd, intgroup = "treatment", returnData = TRUE) pct_var  <- round(100 * attr(pca_data, "percentVar"))  # Build ggplot manually ggplot(pca_data, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = treatment)) +   geom_point(size = 4) +   labs(     x = paste0("PC1 (", pct_var[1], "% variance)"),     y = paste0("PC2 (", pct_var[2], "% variance)"),     color = "Treatment"   ) +   scale_color_manual(values = c("Untreated" = "#4575B4", "Dexamethasone" = "#D73027")) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

title: Code Economy: VISTA vs. Standard R Workflows
text: 16 lines. Manual data preparation, manual label logic, manual threshold lines, manual colour mapping.
code: volcano_df <- res_df %>%   mutate(     neg_log10_p = -log10(pvalue),     label = ifelse(       abs(log2FoldChange) > 2 & padj < 0.01 & !is.na(SYMBOL),       SYMBOL, ""     )   )  ggplot(volcano_df, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = neg_log10_p, color = regulation)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.2) +   geom_text_repel(aes(label = label), size = 3, max.overlaps = 15) +   geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +   geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +   scale_color_manual(values = c(Up = "#D73027", Down = "#1A9850", Other = "grey70")) +   labs(x = "log2 Fold Change", y = "-log10(p-value)", color = "Regulation") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

title: Code Economy: VISTA vs. Standard R Workflows
text: 30 lines. user must: load 2 packages, manually select top genes, compute z-scores, construct HeatmapAnnotation manually repeated colours, map gene symbols row labels, configure Heatmap() 8 parameters.
code: if (requireNamespace("ComplexHeatmap", quietly = TRUE)) {   library(ComplexHeatmap)   library(circlize)    # Select top DE genes   top_genes <- res_df %>%     filter(regulation != "Other") %>%     arrange(padj) %>%     head(50) %>%     pull(gene_id)    # Z-score transform   mat <- norm_mat[top_genes, ]   mat_z <- t(scale(t(log2(mat + 1))))    # Column annotation   col_ann <- HeatmapAnnotation(     Treatment = sample_meta$treatment,     col = list(Treatment = c("Untreated" = "#4575B4", "Dexamethasone" = "#D73027"))   )    # Map gene symbols for labels   row_labels <- ifelse(     !is.na(gene_symbols[top_genes]),     gene_symbols[top_genes],     top_genes   )    Heatmap(     mat_z,     name = "Z-score",     top_annotation = col_ann,     row_labels = row_labels,     show_row_names = TRUE,     row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 7),     column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 9),     clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",     clustering_method_rows = "ward.D2"   ) }

title: Code Economy: VISTA vs. Standard R Workflows
text: 14 lines. user must: filter extract gene symbols manually, know msigdbr column names, construct TERM2GENE data frame, call enricher() correct parameters.
code: # Get upregulated gene symbols up_genes <- res_df %>%   filter(regulation == "Up", !is.na(SYMBOL)) %>%   pull(SYMBOL) %>%   unique()  # Fetch Hallmark gene sets hallmark_sets <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "H") hallmark_t2g  <- hallmark_sets[, c("gs_name", "gene_symbol")]  # Run enrichment enrich_result <- enricher(   gene     = up_genes,   TERM2GENE = hallmark_t2g,   pvalueCutoff = 0.05,   qvalueCutoff = 0.2 )

title: Code Economy: VISTA vs. Standard R Workflows
text: 14 lines. Manual slot extraction, manual factor reordering, manual ggplot2 construction.
code: if (!is.null(enrich_result) && nrow(enrich_result@result) > 0) {   enrich_df <- enrich_result@result %>%     arrange(p.adjust) %>%     head(10) %>%     mutate(       Description = forcats::fct_reorder(Description, -log10(p.adjust)),       neg_log10_fdr = -log10(p.adjust)     )    ggplot(enrich_df, aes(x = neg_log10_fdr, y = Description)) +     geom_point(aes(size = Count, color = neg_log10_fdr)) +     scale_color_gradient(low = "blue", high = "red") +     labs(x = "-log10(FDR)", y = NULL, size = "Gene Count") +     theme_minimal(base_size = 13) }

title: Code Economy: VISTA vs. Standard R Workflows
text: 23 lines (including data preparation shared workflows). create_vista() performed: count filtering, DESeq2 pipeline execution, normalized count extraction, fold-change/p-value thresholding, regulation classification, colour palette assignment, metadata persistence – one call. set_rowdata() handled ID mapping.
code: # Prepare inputs (same as standard workflow) count_data <- as.data.frame(counts_matrix) %>%   tibble::as_tibble() %>%   mutate(gene_id = rownames(counts_matrix)) %>%   select(gene_id, everything())  sample_info <- sample_meta %>%   tibble::as_tibble() %>%   rename(sample_names = Run) %>%   mutate(sample_names = as.character(sample_names))  # One call: DE + filtering + normalization + regulation classification vista <- create_vista(   counts            = count_data,   sample_info       = sample_info,   column_geneid     = "gene_id",   group_column      = "treatment",   group_numerator   = "Dexamethasone",   group_denominator = "Untreated",   method            = "deseq2",   min_counts        = 10,   min_replicates    = 2,   log2fc_cutoff     = 1.0,   pval_cutoff       = 0.05,   p_value_type      = "padj" )  # One call: gene annotation vista <- set_rowdata(   vista,   orgdb   = org.Hs.eg.db,   columns = c("SYMBOL", "GENENAME", "ENTREZID"),   keytype = "ENSEMBL" )

code: palette_table <- colorspace::hcl_palettes(type = "qualitative") |>   as.data.frame() |>   tibble::rownames_to_column("palette") |>   dplyr::select(palette)  n_palettes <- nrow(palette_table)  cat("Number of built-in qualitative palettes available in VISTA:", n_palettes, "\n\n") #> Number of built-in qualitative palettes available in VISTA: 9 palette_table #>    palette #> 1 Pastel 1 #> 2   Dark 2 #> 3   Dark 3 #> 4    Set 2 #> 5    Set 3 #> 6     Warm #> 7     Cold #> 8 Harmonic #> 9  Dynamic palette_grid <- do.call(   rbind,   lapply(palette_table$palette, function(pal) {     cols <- colorspace::qualitative_hcl(8, palette = pal)     data.frame(       palette = pal,       idx = seq_along(cols),       col = cols,       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     )   }) )  palette_grid$palette <- factor(palette_grid$palette, levels = rev(palette_table$palette))  ggplot(palette_grid, aes(x = idx, y = palette, fill = col)) +   geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +   scale_fill_identity() +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:8) +   labs(     x = "Color index within palette",     y = NULL,     title = "VISTA Palette Atlas (Qualitative HCL)"   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

title: Color and Palette Design with VISTA
text: lab journal fixed brand colors, can set explicit named vectors using built-VISTA setters. Available manual setters: set_vista_group_colors(vista, color_map) set_vista_comparison_colors(vista, color_map)
code: custom_group_cols <- c(   control = "#264653",   treatment1 = "#E76F51" )  custom_comp_cols <- c(   treatment1_VS_control = "#6C5CE7",   control_VS_treatment1 = "#00A896" )  vista_custom <- set_vista_group_colors(vista_dark, custom_group_cols) vista_multi_custom <- set_vista_comparison_colors(vista_multi, custom_comp_cols)  group_colors(vista_custom) #>    control treatment1  #>  "#264653"  "#E76F51" S4Vectors::metadata(vista_multi_custom)$comparison$colors #> treatment1_VS_control control_VS_treatment1  #>             "#6C5CE7"             "#00A896" p_custom_group <- get_pca_plot(   vista_custom,   label = FALSE,   point_size = 5 ) + ggtitle("Custom group colors")  p_custom_comp <- get_foldchange_barplot(   vista_multi_custom,   genes = head(rownames(vista_multi_custom), 6),   facet_by = "none" ) + ggtitle("Custom comparison colors")  if (requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)) {   patchwork::wrap_plots(p_custom_group, p_custom_comp, ncol = 2) } else {   p_custom_group   p_custom_comp }

title: Comparing DESeq2 and edgeR with VISTA
text: DESeq2 edgeR two widely used tools differential expression (DE) analysis RNA-seq data. use negative binomial models differ normalization, dispersion estimation, statistical testing, can lead different sets differentially expressed genes (DEGs). vignette demonstrates use VISTA run methods dataset systematically compare results using built-visualization functions.

title: Comparing DESeq2 and edgeR with VISTA
text: create VISTA objects DESeq2 edgeR backends compare DEG counts, fold-change estimates, significance calls identify concordant discordant genes methods visualize method agreement volcano plots, scatter plots, Venn diagrams, heatmaps

title: Comparing DESeq2 and edgeR with VISTA
text: DEG counts method comparison
code: summarise_degs <- function(vista, method_name) {   comps <- comparisons(vista)   do.call(rbind, lapply(names(comps), function(comp) {     de <- as.data.frame(comps[[comp]])     n_up   <- sum(de$regulation == "Up", na.rm = TRUE)     n_down <- sum(de$regulation == "Down", na.rm = TRUE)     data.frame(       Method     = method_name,       Comparison = comp,       Up         = n_up,       Down       = n_down,       Total_DEG  = n_up + n_down,       Tested     = nrow(de)     )   })) }  deg_summary_table <- rbind(   summarise_degs(vista_deseq, "DESeq2"),   summarise_degs(vista_edger, "edgeR") )  knitr::kable(deg_summary_table, row.names = FALSE,              caption = "DEG counts by method and comparison")

title: Comparing DESeq2 and edgeR with VISTA
text: direct comparison fold-change estimates methods reveals overall concordance. Genes diagonal identical estimates; deviations indicate method-specific differences.
code: # Extract DE results for the first comparison de_deseq <- as.data.frame(comparisons(vista_deseq)[[comp1]]) de_edger <- as.data.frame(comparisons(vista_edger)[[comp1]])  # Merge on gene_id merged <- merge(   de_deseq[, c("gene_id", "log2fc", "padj", "regulation")],   de_edger[, c("gene_id", "log2fc", "padj", "regulation")],   by = "gene_id",   suffixes = c("_deseq2", "_edger") )  # Concordance category merged$concordance <- case_when(   merged$regulation_deseq2 == "Up" & merged$regulation_edger == "Up"     ~ "Both Up",   merged$regulation_deseq2 == "Down" & merged$regulation_edger == "Down" ~ "Both Down",   merged$regulation_deseq2 == "Other" & merged$regulation_edger == "Other" ~ "Not DE",   TRUE ~ "Discordant" )  conc_colors <- c(   "Both Up"    = "#D73027",   "Both Down"  = "#4575B4",   "Discordant" = "#FFC107",   "Not DE"     = "grey80" )  # Correlation r_val <- cor(merged$log2fc_deseq2, merged$log2fc_edger,              use = "complete.obs", method = "pearson")  ggplot(merged, aes(x = log2fc_deseq2, y = log2fc_edger, color = concordance)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +   geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +   scale_color_manual(values = conc_colors) +   annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.3,            label = paste0("Pearson r = ", round(r_val, 3)),            fontface = "italic", size = 4) +   labs(     x = "log2 Fold Change (DESeq2)",     y = "log2 Fold Change (edgeR)",     color = "Concordance",     title = paste("Fold-Change Agreement:", comp1)   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: Comparing DESeq2 and edgeR with VISTA
text: Concordance DESeq2 edgeR calls
code: conc_table <- merged %>%   count(concordance) %>%   mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)) %>%   arrange(desc(n))  knitr::kable(conc_table, col.names = c("Category", "Genes", "Percent"),              caption = "Concordance between DESeq2 and edgeR calls")

title: Comparing DESeq2 and edgeR with VISTA
text: Comparing adjusted p-values (-log10 scale) shows whether methods agree genes significant.
code: merged$neg_log10_padj_deseq2 <- -log10(merged$padj_deseq2 + 1e-300) merged$neg_log10_padj_edger  <- -log10(merged$padj_edger + 1e-300)  ggplot(merged, aes(x = neg_log10_padj_deseq2, y = neg_log10_padj_edger,                    color = concordance)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +   geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +   scale_color_manual(values = conc_colors) +   labs(     x = "-log10(padj) DESeq2",     y = "-log10(padj) edgeR",     color = "Concordance",     title = paste("Adjusted P-value Agreement:", comp1)   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: Comparing DESeq2 and edgeR with VISTA
text: distribution raw p-values provides diagnostic method. well-calibrated test produces uniform distribution null, spike near zero truly DE genes.
code: pval_df <- rbind(   data.frame(pvalue = de_deseq$pvalue, Method = "DESeq2"),   data.frame(pvalue = de_edger$pvalue, Method = "edgeR") )  ggplot(pval_df, aes(x = pvalue, fill = Method)) +   geom_histogram(bins = 50, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +   facet_wrap(~Method) +   scale_fill_manual(values = c("DESeq2" = "#1B9E77", "edgeR" = "#D95F02")) +   labs(     x = "Raw P-value",     y = "Count",     title = "P-value Distribution by Method"   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +   theme(legend.position = "none")

title: Comparing DESeq2 and edgeR with VISTA
text: Different significance fold-change thresholds can shift balance methods. sweep across range cutoffs.
code: sweep_cutoffs <- function(de_deseq, de_edger, fc_vals, pval_cut = 0.05) {   results <- lapply(fc_vals, function(fc) {     n_deseq <- sum(       abs(de_deseq$log2fc) >= fc & de_deseq$padj < pval_cut,       na.rm = TRUE     )     n_edger <- sum(       abs(de_edger$log2fc) >= fc & de_edger$padj < pval_cut,       na.rm = TRUE     )     data.frame(       log2fc_cutoff = fc,       DESeq2 = n_deseq,       edgeR  = n_edger     )   })   do.call(rbind, results) }  fc_vals <- seq(0.5, 3, by = 0.25) sweep_df <- sweep_cutoffs(de_deseq, de_edger, fc_vals)  sweep_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(   sweep_df,   cols = c("DESeq2", "edgeR"),   names_to = "Method",   values_to = "n_DEGs" )  ggplot(sweep_long, aes(x = log2fc_cutoff, y = n_DEGs, color = Method)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   geom_point(size = 2) +   scale_color_manual(values = c("DESeq2" = "#1B9E77", "edgeR" = "#D95F02")) +   labs(     x = "|log2FC| Cutoff",     y = "Number of DEGs",     title = "DEG Sensitivity to Fold-Change Threshold",     subtitle = paste("Adjusted p-value <", 0.05)   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 16)

title: Raincloud Plots in VISTA
text: Raincloud plots combine three visual layers: distribution shape (half-violin), robust summary (boxplot), individual observations (jittered points). vignette shows raincloud plotting expression fold-change data VISTA, including line-connection control id.long.var optional statistical annotations.

title: Raincloud Plots in VISTA
code: library(VISTA) library(ggplot2)  data("count_data", package = "VISTA") data("sample_metadata", package = "VISTA")  # Keep runtime modest for vignette rendering count_small <- count_data[1:1000, ]  vista <- create_vista(   counts = count_small,   sample_info = sample_metadata,   column_geneid = "gene_id",   group_column = "cond_long",   group_numerator = "treatment1",   group_denominator = "control",   method = "deseq2",   min_counts = 10,   min_replicates = 1 )  comp_names <- names(comparisons(vista)) top_up <- get_genes_by_regulation(   vista,   sample_comparisons = comp_names[1],   regulation = "Up" ) n_select_genes = 50 selected_genes <- stats::na.omit(utils::head(top_up$gene_id, n_select_genes)) if (!length(selected_genes)) {   selected_genes <- rownames(vista)[1:n_select_genes] }

title: Raincloud Plots in VISTA
code: get_expression_raincloud(   vista,   genes = selected_genes[1:10],   value_transform = "log2",   summarise = FALSE,   facet_by = "none" )

title: Raincloud Plots in VISTA
text: expression rainclouds: summarise = FALSE: point gene-sample value (pooled across selected genes). summarise = TRUE: point gene-level group summary (one value per gene per group). summarise = TRUE, using id.long.var = "gene" useful connecting gene across groups.
code: get_expression_raincloud(   vista,   genes = selected_genes[1:10],   value_transform = "log2",   summarise = FALSE,   facet_by = "none",   id.long.var = "gene" ) get_expression_raincloud(   vista,   genes = selected_genes[1:10],   value_transform = "log2",   summarise = TRUE,   facet_by = "none",   id.long.var = "gene" )

what: Expression raincloud with lines and p-values
title: Raincloud Plots in VISTA
code: get_expression_raincloud(   vista,   genes = selected_genes[1:10],   value_transform = "log2",   summarise = TRUE,   facet_by = "none",   id.long.var = "gene",   stats_group = TRUE,   stats_method = "wilcox.test",   p.label = "p.format" )

title: Raincloud Plots in VISTA
text: object symbol annotations rowData(vista) (provide display_from/display_orgdb), can label directly symbol space: facet_by = "gene", prefer summarise = FALSE facet retains replicate-level distribution. summarise = TRUE, facet group-level summaries raincloud shape usually informative.
code: get_expression_raincloud(   vista,   genes = selected_genes[1:10],   value_transform = "log2",   summarise = TRUE,   facet_by = "none",   label = TRUE,   label_column = "gene",   label_size = 3 ) get_expression_raincloud(   vista,   genes = c("NFKBIA", "KLF6", "PER1"),   value_transform = "log2",   summarise = TRUE,   facet_by = "none",   label = TRUE,   display_id = "SYMBOL" ) get_expression_raincloud(   vista,   genes = selected_genes[1:2],   value_transform = "log2",   summarise = FALSE,   facet_by = "gene",   label = TRUE,   label_column = "gene",   label_size = 2.8 )

what: Why this is harder outside VISTA
title: Raincloud Plots in VISTA
text: Outside VISTA, producing equivalent raincloud plots involved must manually: extract harmonize DE tables per comparison, reshape long format plotting, track grouping palette consistency, map repeated-measure identifiers line connections, add control statistical annotations per plotting context. minimal non-VISTA workflow typically requires custom wrangling multiple plot-specific settings: VISTA, steps encapsulated get_expression_raincloud() get_foldchange_raincloud() staying consistent rest plotting API.
code: # 1) Build long expression/fold-change tables manually # 2) Join sample metadata and comparison metadata # 3) Validate IDs for repeated measures (id.long.var) # 4) Create raincloud layers and palette mapping # 5) Add statistical comparisons and label formatting # 6) Repeat the process for each analysis object/comparison set

title: VISTA Function Reference

Arguments: counts: Raw counts (matrix/data.frame) gene ID column + sample columns. sample_info: Sample metadata sample_names matching rownames. column_geneid: Column name counts holds gene identifiers. group_column: Column sample_info used group samples. group_numerator: Numerator group(s) comparisons. group_denominator: Denominator group(s), length/order numerator. method: "deseq2" (default), "edger", "limma", "". min_counts: Minimum total counts per gene retain. min_replicates: Minimum samples per group meeting min_counts. log2fc_cutoff: Absolute LFC threshold DEG calling. pval_cutoff: P‑value cutoff. p_value_type: "padj" "pvalue" (create_vista() controls DE calling across methods). covariates: Optional additive covariate columns sample_info. design_formula: Optional explicit design formula including group_column. consensus_mode: method = "", "intersection" "union". consensus_log2fc: consensus tables, log2fc populated. result_source: Active DE source ("consensus", "deseq2", "edger", "limma"). group_palette: Colorspace palette name group colors. comparison_palette: Palette name comparison colors. validate: Run full object validation return.

title: Visualization and Integrated System for Transcriptomic Analysis
text: VISTA Bioconductor-oriented framework RNA-seq differential expression analysis keeps data, statistics, annotations, visualization single SummarizedExperiment-based object. designed analysts want reproducible workflow without rebuilding plotting result-handling code every project. VISTA provides: single entry point DESeq2, edgeR, limma-voom, DESeq2/edgeR consensus workflow. Design-aware modeling covariates explicit design formula. Publication-ready visualizations QC, differential expression, expression patterns, fold-change structure, pathway enrichment, deconvolution. Consistent color management across comparisons groups. Export helpers YAML-driven Quarto reporting workflow shareable analyses.

title: Visualization and Integrated System for Transcriptomic Analysis
text: RNA-seq projects repeat sequence steps: normalize counts, fit differential models, extract contrasts, make QC plots, label genes, summarize pathways, assemble figures collaborators. friction usually statistics alone; repeated glue code connects . VISTA addresses organizing workflow around one validated object: assay(x) stores normalized expression data. rowData(x) stores feature annotations. colData(x) stores sample metadata. comparisons(x) stores differential expression tables. VISTA accessors plotting functions operate directly object. design makes easier move raw counts consistent analysis narrative without switching data structures step.

title: Run Differential Expression Analysis with DESeq2, edgeR, or limma-voom — run_deseq_analysis
text: counts data frame matrix raw counts one gene per row. Must include column defined column_geneid, column names must match entries sample_info$sample_names. sample_info data frame sample metadata. Must contain sample_names specified grouping column. column_geneid string identifying column name containing gene identifiers. group_column name column sample_info defines experimental groups. group_numerator character vector numerator group(s) fold-change comparisons. group_denominator character vector denominator group(s) fold-change comparisons. covariates Optional character vector additional sample_info columns adjust . design_formula Optional model formula (formula string). provided, overrides automatic design construction group_column + covariates. Must include group_column. min_counts Minimum total read count across samples retain gene. Default: 10. min_replicates Minimum number replicates within group must exceed min_counts. Default: 1. log2fc_cutoff Absolute log2 fold-change threshold define DEGs. Default: 1. pval_cutoff P-value adjusted p-value cutoff significance. Default: 0.05. p_value_type DESeq2: one "padj" "pvalue". edgeR/limma: one "FDR" "PValue".

title: Run Differential Expression Analysis with DESeq2, edgeR, or limma-voom — run_deseq_analysis
text: named list components: norm_counts: Matrix normalized expression values (CPM edgeR/limma, DESeq2-normalized counts). sample_info: Updated sample metadata. row_data: Gene-level metadata, including mean expression. comparisons: Named list DEG result tibbles (one per comparison), containing standardized columns: gene_id, log2fc, pvalue, p.adj, regulation. deg_summary: List summary tables showing DEG regulation counts.

title: Run Differential Expression Analysis with DESeq2, edgeR, or limma-voom — run_deseq_analysis
text: Perform differential expression (DE) analysis across multiple group comparisons using DESeq2, edgeR, limma-voom. functions process raw count data, normalize , execute pairwise group-level tests, return standardized DEG outputs compatible VISTA-based visualization analysis. DESeq2, normalization performed via DESeq, DE testing uses results. edgeR, normalization uses calcNormFactors, testing uses glmLRT. limma, normalization uses calcNormFactors + voom, testing uses eBayes. Low-abundance filtering applied model fitting. Gene regulation status determined via .categorize_deg_results() based user thresholds. output comparison results internally standardized via .tidy_de_results() ensure uniform column schema compatible VISTA plotting tools.

title: Run Differential Expression Analysis with DESeq2, edgeR, or limma-voom — run_deseq_analysis

title: Set or append rowData annotations on a VISTA object — set_rowdata
text: x VISTA object. annotations Optional data.frame/tibble/DataFrame one row per gene column containing gene IDs match rownames(x). omitted, annotations pulled orgdb. orgdb Optional OrgDb object; supplied (annotations NULL), annotations retrieved via AnnotationDbi::select(). key_col Name column annotations holds gene IDs. Default: c("SYMBOL","GENENAME","ENSEMBL","ENTREZID","TXCHROM","TXSTART","TXEND"). TXCHROM/TXSTART/TXEND fields carry basic genomic coordinates available OrgDb. drop_version Logical; TRUE, strips Ensembl version suffixes (e.g., .1) VISTA rownames key column/keys matching. overwrite Logical; TRUE, replaces existing rowData.
